findings.impact: Implementation can satisfy fail-closed rules by returning incomplete for every run, leaving the requested portable test runner unusable without this being discovered until late.
findings.text: The design promises an ordinary-Git, unprivileged committed-target execution path but does not identify a concrete viable mechanism on any supported platform that maintains immutable inputs or reliably observes every modification and loss of coverage for the whole run. A private temporary checkout or read-only file permissions alone are expressly insufficient because the test process or another same-user process can modify and revert input bytes. Define an initial supported-platform mechanism and early real-platform feasibility test demonstrating both a passing full run and invalidation on edit-and-revert/observation loss, or bring the owner a concrete tradeoff if none is feasible.

not: A new graph service, a replacement test runner or a separately implemented multilingual parser.

spec: Implement the shared deterministic helper and a real repository adapter per docs/test-impact/design.md sections 2–5, 7–10 and 13–14. Require explicit exact endpoints and enforce execution snapshot identity, including reliable detection of relevant input mutations. Discover and map actual runner targets, include changed tests, apply declared invalidation and full fallback rules, preserve original full workflows and gates, report separate impact, plan, execution and verification statuses, and implement compatible baseline receipts and receipt chaining. Missing or incompatible baseline expands execution to the full configured profile. Include meaningful acceptance tests for the snapshot, discovery, fallback, evidence, error and execution contracts. Select a representative project and runner through design; no model invocation in normal runs. The full design is binding. Work directly in this fork for an eventual upstream pull request; no separate product repository or subtree. Owner scope clarification: Initial release requires explicit committed Git endpoints only, and must work across platforms and filesystems with ordinary Git repositories, without Btrfs, privileged operations, special mounts or subvolumes. Worktree target support is deferred; reject it clearly rather than silently substituting a commit. Preserve exact target execution identity and protection against mutations, and adapt the original worktree-specific acceptance cases accordingly.
